title: What Should the Rules for A.I. Companies Actually Be? We Asked the Experts.
content:
What should the government do? We asked a panel of experts to assess the risks A.I. presents and the tools of governance that could be adopted to address them.

Kate Brennan, a former Google tech worker, leads the policy agenda on A.I. and corporate power at the AI Now Institute, an independent research institute providing expert analysis on A.I. in the public interest.

Brennan: Here’s what I see as the biggest risk: These companies are spending so much money on building out this technology. The consulting firm Bain estimates that by 2031, they will have to achieve $6 trillion of revenue annually to sustain their current level of capital expenditure, which is $1.5 trillion a year. In order for those numbers to add up in any way, they need to push this tech everywhere, into all of our public institutions and contracting, including in areas where A.I. is not fit for purpose, is not secure, safe by design. That’s what we should be talking about.

Brennan: Government is supposed to stop harmful products from entering the market. We do it with drugs. We do it with airplanes. The issue here is corporate negligence. That should be the focus.

title: A.I.’s Rogue Behavior Starts With Its Training
content:
But security researchers pointed out that the Hugging Face breach was largely preventable with standard cybersecurity protocols. Boyan Milanov, a senior research scientist at the AI Now Institute who specializes in evaluating A.I.’s cybersecurity risks, said safety must be enforced by “having a properly designed test environment that doesn’t allow the agent’s program to perform the actions that are unwanted and potentially harmful.”

Experts argue that the inherent difficulty of containment — because of imperfect sandboxes or agents taking unintended actions — does not absolve companies of responsibility. “The rogue A.I. narrative is so useful for these companies because it absolves them from the responsibility in these incidents,” Mr. Milanov said.

title: COP31 pledge on AI lacks climate targets, critics say
content:
The pledge doesn’t acknowledge the link with fossil fuels, even as the data center boom threatens tech companies’ pledges to reduce planet-warming emissions. Some experts worry that part of the pledge plays into an industry narrative, which asserts that data center impacts can be mitigated by using AI to address climate change.

“We have seen over many, many years that voluntary pledges are not enough and that self-regulation by industry does not work — we can’t trust them to grade their own homework,” said Alli Finn, head of community partnerships at AI Now Institute, a nonprofit that studies the societal effects of AI.

Read the full article here.

title: The big tech defectors you’re not hearing about
content:
In other words, it’s been a worrying spell for anyone who’s concerned about the still ascendant power of the tech oligarchy. Fortunately, people are fighting back. Earlier this week, I went to New York for the AI People’s Assembly, an event put on by AI Now, where I’m a journalist in residence, and More Perfect Union.

It was a loaded bill, and participants included Mayor Zoran Mamdani, Lena Khan, multiple data center opposition organizers, and friends of Blood in the Machine, like Karen Howe, Bina DuBall, and Naomi Klein. The event was held at Webster Hall, and the line stretched out the door like a rock show, and it was a reminder that the appetite for resisting the AI oligarchy is larger than ever, and countless people are ready to meet the moment.

title: The Bots Are Just The Closers
content:
On Monday night, I was at Webster Hall in New York for the People’s AI Assembly, hosted by the AI Now Institute and More Perfect Union. The sold-out event featured a wide range of speakers, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Ilana Glazer, and KeShaun Pearson.

But the room also mattered. Webster Hall has been a gathering place since 1886. Workers have organized strikes there. Activists rallied there to defend immigrants on trial. Queer New Yorkers threw drag balls there that are still legendary. And this week, the space filled up with people who refuse the future the AI industry is selling us.

Read the full piece here.

title: Amid AI Boom, “Risk Is Spreading Throughout the Economy”: Astra Taylor & Naomi Klein
content:
We’re joined by Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor, co-authors of the book End Times Fascism, for a wide-ranging conversation on the multitrillion-dollar global investment in artificial intelligence and its reverberating effects around the world.

Klein recently spoke at the People’s AI Assembly, alongside other critics of the artificial intelligence industry, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and former chair of the Federal Trade Commission Lina Khan. “The resistance to AI is taking many forms, and it’s really a resistance to oligarch power, which is concentrated in the hands of these tech companies,” Klein tells Democracy Now! “After 50 years of outsourcing and hollowing out of public functions of the state, the very last stage is the outsourcing of thinking, of intelligence itself.”

Watch the full segment here.

title: Zohran Mamdani Backs Major Expansion of New York’s Data Center Moratorium
content:
Speaking on stage at the AI Now Institute and More Perfect Union’s “People’s AI Assembly,” actress and advocate Ilana Glazer asked the New York City mayor if he would push Gov. Hochul to sign the “Responsible Data Center Development Act,” which passed New York state legislation earlier this year; Mamdani responded with a simple and resolute “yes.”

[…]

Numerous surveys find that anti-AI and specifically anti-data-center sentiments have grown nationwide over the past year. This collective anxiety over AI development was palpable on Monday night at the “People’s AI Assembly,” where the entry line at New York City’s Webster Hall wrapped comfortably around the block. Attendees included college students holding “no data center” signs in hand, concerned parents of school-age children facing a future seemingly inundated with AI, and even some tech workers employed by the very companies selling the technology.

title: Mamdani says feds have abdicated on AI, urges New Yorkers to push back
content:
Two of New York’s sweethearts, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and activist and “Broad City” star Ilana Glazer, spoke about AI at Webster Hall in Manhattan on Monday night, with Glazer posing questions to the mayor about the future of AI in society.  

[…]

His message came at a moment when the federal government is doing little to regulate AI, leaving cities to act on their own. At The People’s AI Assembly, an event hosted by the AI Now Institute, a think tank that explores the social implications of AI, Mamdani argued that the technology’s rapid rollout is not inevitable and that public officials should hold AI companies accountable.
